paper_diagnosis: Disseminated cryptococcal infection in a patient who had kidney transplant
disease_label_per_paper: Cryptococcal meningitis and fungaemia two months after kidney transplantation
presentation_summary: 29-year-old man with congenital cystinosis two months after third kidney transplant presented with frontal headache and a single fever episode.
He had received basiliximab induction, high-dose prednisolone boluses followed by taper to 5 mg/day, tacrolimus, and mycophenolate mofetil.
Admission exam was otherwise unremarkable with body temperature 36.4 C; labs showed no leukocytosis and no elevated CRP.
Brain MRI showed meningeal irritation; lumbar puncture had normal opening pressure but mild CSF pleocytosis and elevated CSF lactate/albumin.
India ink showed high encapsulated yeast load; cryptococcal antigen was positive in CSF and blood; C. neoformans grew from CSF and all blood cultures.
He received liposomal amphotericin B plus flucytosine for 2 weeks and prolonged fluconazole consolidation; follow-up at 3 years was good.
